# Dependence components, shape propagation, and graph recession transfer

These lemmas concern finite convexity spaces induced by Euclidean point
sets. They prove a compactification mechanism but do not prove a sharp
mixed centerpoint theorem.

## 1. Canonical dependence components

Let P be a nonempty finite subset of a Euclidean space, Q=conv(P), and
let F_z be the minimal face of Q containing z. For each nonvertex z of
Q, take the hyperedge E_z=P∩F_z. The equivalence classes generated by
these hyperedges are the dependence components P_1,...,P_s; vertices
belonging to no nontrivial hyperedge are singleton components.

These are also the components generated by every nontrivial convex
representation z=Σ_w λ_w w with z,w∈P. Every source of such a
representation lies in F_z, by the defining supporting equations of
that face. Conversely, for every nonvertex z, there is a representation
of z with strictly positive coefficients at every point of
(P∩F_z)\{z}. Indeed, z is in the relative interior of the convex hull of
that set. Give each of its finitely many points an initially small
positive coefficient; the residual point remains in that convex hull
when these coefficients are sufficiently small. Represent the residual
point and add its nonnegative coefficients. For rational P the chosen
coefficients may be rational.

Write cl_P(A)=P∩conv(A). Then, for every A⊂P,

    cl_P(A) = ⋃_i cl_{P_i}(A∩P_i).                         (1)

To prove the nontrivial inclusion, represent z∈cl_P(A) using A. If the
representation uses z itself, remove its coefficient unless it is one;
in the latter case z∈A and the conclusion is immediate. Every remaining
source belongs to the component of z by the preceding characterization.
This proves (1). In particular each component is P-closed. If P is
lattice-convex, each P_i is lattice-convex as well.

## 2. Exact Helly additivity

Let h(P) be the least h such that every finite family of ambient convex
sets whose total intersection misses P has a subfamily of at most h
with that property. For a finite P it is enough to use P-closed traces:
every such trace A is realized by conv(A), and every trace of a convex
set is P-closed. Also h(P)≤|P|, by choosing one excluding set per point.

**Lemma.** The dependence components satisfy

    h(P) = Σ_i h(P_i).                                    (2)

For the upper bound, choose at most h(P_i) members of a given infeasible
family whose intersection misses P_i, then take the union of these
subfamilies. For the lower bound, choose a minimal infeasible family of
h(P_i) closed traces on P_i; such a family exists by the definition of
the finite integer h(P_i). Extend each trace by every other component.
Equation (1) makes each extension P-closed. The resulting union of
families is infeasible, and removing any one member leaves a common
point in its original component. Its size is Σ_i h(P_i), proving (2).

In particular, for finite lattice-convex P⊂Z^n, Doignon gives
Σ_i h(P_i)≤2^n. This additivity by itself does not prove a γ_d/h(P_i)
continuous-fiber bound for a component.

## 3. Uniform propagation of diameters

Suppose K_z⊂R^d, z∈P, are nonempty compact convex sets and satisfy all
actual compatibility inclusions

    Σ_w λ_w K_w ⊂ K_z  whenever z=Σ_w λ_w w.               (3)

Assume every fiber volume is between v>0 and V<∞. Choose once and for
all the finite strictly positive representations from Section 1, and
let λ_*>0 be the smallest coefficient appearing in them. Singleton
components need no coefficients or propagation.

Suppose a source K_u in one such representation has diameter at most D.
Fix arbitrary points in the other source fibers. The target contains a
translate B of λ_u K_u. Center a ball at any point of B. Then

    B⊂λ_u D B_d,    |B|≥λ_u^d v.

The cone-volume lemma in
`candidate 2a5bf571e6159901`, applied about that
center, gives

    diam(K_z) ≤ 2D(1+2dV/(λ_*^d v)).                      (4)

Each source λ_w K_w has a translate contained in K_z, so
diam(K_w)≤diam(K_z)/λ_w. Alternatively, if the already bounded node is
the target, this last inclusion immediately bounds all sources.

Consequently one reached node in a hyperedge bounds every node of that
edge. Put

    B_* = (2/λ_*) (1+2dV/(λ_*^d v)).

After normalizing one positive anchor fiber in a component by the
determinant-one maximal-simplex map, all fibers in that component have
diameter at most

    2 sqrt(d) (d!V)^(1/d) B_*^(|P_i|-1).                  (5)

At most |P_i|-1 expansions adding a previously unreached node are
needed. Formula (5) is intentionally a loose uniform bound. It tracks
diameters only: no bounded positions or ordinary affine-shear removal
are asserted here.

For a sequence, the assumption v>0 is available after restricting to
the support of positive limiting normalized fiber masses. Such a
support T is P-closed: if z is a convex combination of indices of T,
one positive source, of coefficient λ, gives |K_z|≥λ^d|K_w| by fixing
points in the other sources. Hence z also has positive limiting mass.

## 4. Universal graph and exact preservation of representations

Let L(P) be the space of scalar functions g on P satisfying

    g(z)=Σ_w λ_w g(w) whenever z=Σ_w λ_w w.               (6)

It includes constants and all restricted affine coordinate functions.
Choose a basis 1,g_1,...,g_{ℓ-1}, and set
Φ(z)=(g_1(z),...,g_{ℓ-1}(z)). Its affine span has dimension ℓ-1.
The original coordinates z are affine functions of Φ(z), so Φ is
injective and admits an affine projection back to P.

An anchored convex representation in P lifts to the identical
representation in Φ(P), by (6). Conversely, an anchored representation
in Φ(P) projects to one in P. Therefore representations, closed traces,
and Helly numbers are preserved exactly. Moreover

    L(Φ(P)) = Aff(Φ(P)),   h(Φ(P))=h(P).                  (7)

Indeed the functions respecting the preserved representations are
precisely L(P); the chosen basis makes all of them restrictions of
affine functions on Φ(P).

## 5. Subtracting divergent modes without losing actual compatibility

Suppose all fiber diameters are bounded by D. Choose their centroids
c_z. Fix a finite matrix T whose kernel is L(P), using rows
e_z−(λ_w)_w from vertices of the finite anchored-representation
polytopes. Every such row obeys

    |c_z−Σ_w λ_w c_w|≤D,                                 (8)

because both displayed points belong to K_z by (3). If T has m rows
and smallest nonzero singular value σ, its elementary orthogonal
decomposition gives

    dist(c,L(P)⊗R^d) ≤ D sqrt(m)/σ.                       (9)

If T=0 the distance is zero. Let g_z be the orthogonal projection of
c onto L(P)⊗R^d, and put R_z=K_z−g_z. All R_z lie in one fixed ball,
by (9) and the diameter bound. They remain an actual family: translating
(3) by −g_z and using (6) proves every required inclusion exactly.
No assertion that these translations preserve halfspaces is made.

Instead form the lifted family

    S^lift = {(Φ(z),x): z∈P, x∈R_z}.                     (10)

It is actual over the finite base Φ(P), because the anchored
representations are the same. Each g_z is an affine vector-valued
function G(Φ(z)). The affine map

    (t,x) ↦ (π(t), x+G(t))                               (11)

sends (10) precisely onto the original family. Here π is the affine
projection from Φ(P) to P.

## 6. Depth transfer with bounded residual fibers retained

Give either family the sum of the d-dimensional volumes of its fibers.
The affine map (11) is a translation on each residual fiber, hence
preserves this measure. It need not be injective on the whole ambient
space. Every containing halfspace in the image pulls back to a
containing halfspace in the lifted ambient space, or to its entirety.
Consequently, pointwise,

    depth_original(z,x+g_z) ≥ depth_lifted(Φ(z),x).        (12)

This uses arbitrary residual convex fibers, not compatible centroids
or any common target distribution.

For a sequence of residual families contained in a fixed ball, take a
simultaneous Hausdorff limit. Convex-body indicators converge in L1,
including zero-volume limits, and there are finitely many fibers, so
the mixed measures converge in total variation. Candidate movement
within one fixed residual fiber changes depth by at most

    |P| κ_{d-1} R^(d-1) |x−x'| / M,

where all residual fibers lie in R B_d and M is their positive total
mass. Normalize a nonzero continuous halfspace normal to unit length
and bound every threshold-change slab by its maximal section area to
obtain this inequality; purely base-direction halfspaces are unchanged.
Thus maximum depths of the lifted residual families converge. Combining
this with (12) gives

    liminf_j max depth_original,j ≥ max depth_lifted,limit. (13)

For the particular recession K_j,z=jg(z)e_1+R_j,z, the simpler lift
(z,g(z),x) and map (z,t,x)↦(z,jt e_1+x) suffice. Equation (13) includes
all closed ambient halfspaces and their boundary mass. Its validity
depends on retaining the full residual fibers. Replacing them by
weighted graph atoms is a different operation and has no such claim.

## 7. Exact scope of the reduction

Within a component having uniformly positive limiting masses, (5),
(9), and the universal lift give compact residual families and (13),
while preserving the component Helly number. Disconnected components
have the exact budget (2); if a γ_d/h theorem were proved for each
component, selecting one with maximal mass divided by h would prove
that theorem for their union. Neither that sharp theorem nor a
variational argument proving it is supplied here.
